title: Microsoft 365: Frontier program expands to preview features in Teams, Outlook, OneDrive and SharePoint
summary: The roadmap facts, enrolment controls, licensing qualifications and preview terms are supported. The Autopilot description should retain Microsoft's qualification about automated action review and required approvals.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Users need licences covering the products they preview.
claims.quote: Assign users licenses that provide access to the products you want them to preview.

claims.quote: to use Frontier features for Copilot, users need a Microsoft Copilot license or a license that includes access to Copilot.

claims.claim: Teams Frontier features require a licence including Teams.
claims.quote: to use Frontier features for Microsoft Teams, users need a license that includes access to Teams.

claims.claim: Enrolled users lacking the matching product licence are not shown the corresponding Frontier features.
claims.quote: Users enrolled in Frontier without a Microsoft Copilot license aren't presented with Copilot-related Frontier features. ... Users enrolled in Frontier without a license that includes access to Teams aren't presented with Teams-related Frontier features.

claims.claim: The admin's corresponding product licence is recommended for full visibility of Frontier AI settings and agents.
claims.quote: Verify that your own admin account has also has a corresponding license for products to ensure full access to Frontier AI settings and agents. Some Frontier settings and agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center might not appear.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Frontier is an audience for access to features before general availability, including agents.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Frontier program gives organizations preview access ... before those features reach general availability (GA). By opting in to Frontier, IT administrators can evaluate new Microsoft Copilot agents

claims.claim: Standard release is the default for generally available features.
claims.quote: For general availability updates, the default release preference for your organization is Standard release.

claims.claim: Deferred release delays deferred-eligible major updates approximately 30 days after Standard rollout begins.
claims.quote: Deferred release lets you delay deferred-eligible major updates for specific users for approximately 30 days after rollout to the Standard release audience begins.

claims.claim: Updates ineligible for Deferred release follow the Standard schedule.
claims.quote: updates that aren't eligible for Deferred release aren't delayed and these updates are released to Deferred release users on the same schedule as Standard release.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Users can be opted into Frontier while also assigned to Standard or Deferred release.
claims.quote: You can opt in users to both Frontier preview and assign them to Standard release or Deferred release.

claims.claim: For features outside Frontier, existing Standard or Deferred preferences determine delivery at GA.
claims.quote: For features that aren't part of Frontier, the user's existing Standard release or Deferred release preference determines when they receive features at GA.

claims.claim: The unified experience rolls out gradually from mid-November 2026 and may not yet be available in a tenant.
claims.quote: The unified release preferences experience is rolling out gradually in mid-November 2026, so it might not be available in your organization yet.

claims.claim: The existing Copilot Frontier enrolment experience remains after the unified experience arrives.
claims.quote: When the unified release preferences experience becomes available, the existing experience for opting in to Frontier preview within the Microsoft 365 admin center will still exist.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout

claims.quote: Frontier features are preview and subject to change.

claims.claim: Some Frontier features require models from AI providers such as Anthropic.
claims.quote: Some Frontier features and agents require access to large language models from AI providers, such as Anthropic.

claims.claim: Frontier never enables AI providers on the administrator's behalf.
claims.quote: Frontier will never enable AI providers on your behalf.

claims.quote: If the corresponding AI provider isn't enabled by you, the Frontier feature will not be usable for you or your users. To allow access to other models, use the Microsoft 365 admin center to explicitly approve each model.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Frontier does not override Agent settings; an agent disabled in the Agent view stays unavailable regardless of enrolment.
claims.quote: The Frontier admin control doesn't override the settings configured in the Agent section of the admin center. If an admin turned off a Frontier agent in the Agent view, that agent isn't available to users, regardless of a user's Frontier enrollment.

claims.claim: Starting March 29, 2026, newly published Frontier agents are available only to Frontier-enrolled users.
claims.quote: Starting March 29, 2026, newly published Frontier agents are available only to Frontier-enrolled users.

claims.claim: Frontier agents published before March 29, 2026 remain accessible to all users with a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Frontier agents published before this date continue to be accessible to all users with a Microsoft Copilot license.

claims.claim: Frontier agents appear in the Agent store with (Frontier) in their names.
claims.quote: Frontier agents are available to them from the Agent store in Microsoft Copilot. Search for "Built by Microsoft", and Frontier program agents are displayed with (Frontier) in the name.

claims.claim: Autopilot uses authorised Teams, Outlook, OneDrive and SharePoint information through available tools.
claims.quote: Autopilot uses authorized Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, and SharePoint information through its available tools.

claims.claim: Autopilot can complete tasks without asking at each step.
claims.quote: Autopilot can complete tasks without asking at each step. ... Actions that match the owner's request run; others show an approval card. Payments and sensitive browser steps always need approval.
claims.fix: Append: 'An automated review system reviews actions that send, share, delete or change content, or create or change an automation; actions matching the owner's request run, others show an approval card, and payments and sensitive browser steps always need approval.' Keep the existing application-card citation.

claims.claim: Moving users from Standard to Deferred may remove access to features not yet available in Deferred.
claims.quote: If you move users from Standard release to Deferred release, they might lose access to features that aren't available yet in Deferred release.

claims.claim: Deferred release and Frontier are currently unavailable in GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: For customers in GCC, GCC High, and DoD environments ... Currently, Deferred release and Frontier aren't available in government cloud environments.

claims.claim: The release model applies to new Outlook for Windows, Outlook on the web, OneDrive, SharePoint Online, Office for the web, Teams and the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: The Microsoft 365 updates described in this article apply to New Outlook for Windows, Outlook on the web, OneDrive, SharePoint Online, Office for the web, Microsoft Teams, and the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: These release options exclude Microsoft 365 Apps, which use separate update channels.
claims.quote: These updates don't apply to Microsoft 365 Apps, which are managed separately via update channels

claims.claim: Targeted release retires in January 2027.
claims.quote: In January 2027, Targeted release will be retired and no longer available to use.

claims.claim: Existing Frontier users stay enrolled after Targeted release retirement.
claims.quote: If you already have users enrolled in Frontier, these users will stay enrolled in Frontier after the retirement of Targeted release.

claims.claim: From November 2026, commercial clouds can no longer add, remove or modify Targeted release enrolment.
claims.quote: In November 2026, commercial clouds can no longer add users to, remove users from, or modify Targeted release enrollment.

claims.claim: The previous Standard and Deferred management experience retires in commercial clouds when the unified experience arrives.
claims.quote: The previous experience for managing Standard release and Deferred release preferences will be retired for commercial clouds when the unified release preferences experience becomes available.

claims.claim: The unified Frontier control is in Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Release preferences > Turn on Frontier.
claims.quote: go to Settings > Org settings. ... Under the Organization profile tab, select Release preferences. ... To opt in to Frontier preview, toggle Turn on Frontier to On.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for unified Frontier audience enrolment is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Frontier enrollment Turn on Frontier Microsoft Graph beta PowerShell release preferences Standard Deferred API; Copilot Frontier PowerShell Graph. Read get-started-frontier and graph/utcm-copilot-resources: the latter configures OCPS tenant policies, not enrolment audiences.

claims.claim: The existing control is in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot Frontier > Turn on Frontier.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Settings. ... Select the View all tab. ... Select Copilot Frontier. ... To opt in to Frontier preview, toggle Turn on Frontier to On.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the existing Copilot Frontier enrolment control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Frontier PowerShell Graph; Frontier enrollment Graph PowerShell. Read get-started-frontier and graph/utcm-copilot-resources: microsoft.copilot.frontier is an OCPS web-app policy, not the Copilot enrolment audience setting.

claims.claim: The unified GA control is in Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Organization profile > Release preferences > Standard release or Deferred release.
claims.quote: go to Settings > Org settings. ... Under the Organization profile tab, select Release preferences. ... From the Release preferences panel, choose either Standard release or Deferred release.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for Standard or Deferred release assignment is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 organization release preferences Standard Deferred release PowerShell Graph API settings; Standard Deferred release preferences API. Read configure-release-options and search excerpts from release-options-faq and release-options-in-office-365; no assignment call found.

claims.claim: Standard or Deferred release allows up to 10,000 user exceptions.
claims.quote: You can add up to 10,000 exceptions to Standard release or Deferred release.

claims.claim: Each group member and individually assigned user counts toward the 10,000-user limit.
claims.quote: Each user in a security group and each user added individually count toward the 10,000-user limit.

claims.claim: AI Administrator can configure Standard and Deferred release.
claims.quote: To configure Standard release and Deferred release options, you need one of the following roles in the Microsoft 365 admin center: ... AI Admin

claims.claim: Security Administrator can configure Standard and Deferred release.
claims.quote: To configure Standard release and Deferred release options, you need one of the following roles in the Microsoft 365 admin center: ... Security Admin

claims.claim: Office Apps Administrator can configure Standard and Deferred release.
claims.quote: To configure Standard release and Deferred release options, you need one of the following roles in the Microsoft 365 admin center: ... Office Apps Admin

claims.where: Governance controls: Standard and Deferred paragraph
claims.claim: Before the unified experience arrives, GA preferences are at Copilot > Settings > View all > Copilot Release Preferences: General Availability > Standard release or Deferred release.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Settings. ... Under the View all tab, select Copilot Release Preferences: General Availability. ... Choose either Standard release or Deferred release.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs admins to Agent > Settings > Agent and plugin access > Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agent > Settings > Agent and plugin access. ... Verify that Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft is checked.

claims.claim: Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft must be checked to allow Frontier agents.
claims.quote: Before your users can access Frontier agents, make sure that agent types are approved for use. ... This setting allows the use of Microsoft Frontier agents.

claims.where: Governance controls: Standard and Deferred paragraph
claims.claim: The unified Release preferences panel manages Frontier separately from GA release selection.
claims.quote: Release preferences for Frontier, Standard release, and Deferred release can now be managed through the unified release preferences experience ... To opt in to Frontier preview, toggle Turn on Frontier to On.

claims.claim: The cited Frontier and release-options pages document admin steps but no PowerShell or Graph call for these enrolment and release settings.
claims.quote: Searched: Frontier enrollment Turn on Frontier Microsoft Graph beta PowerShell; Microsoft 365 organization release preferences Standard Deferred release PowerShell Graph API settings. Opened get-started-frontier and configure-release-options in full; neither documents these calls.

claims.claim: The Frontier page publishes no price or credit rate for a specific preview.
claims.quote: Searched: get-started-frontier price credit rate budget cap. Read get-started-frontier in full: it says some experiences may be paid and links the Copilot Credits Guide, but supplies no specific preview price or rate.

claims.claim: The Frontier page describes no cap or budget control.
claims.quote: Searched: get-started-frontier price credit rate budget cap. Read get-started-frontier in full: no cap or budget control is described there. The Autopilot application card separately describes spending policies; the briefing's absence is limited to the Frontier page.

claims.claim: Learn says IT administrators control which users have access to which Frontier features.
claims.quote: IT admins have explicit control which users have access to which Frontier features.

claims.claim: The Frontier page refers readers to the Microsoft Copilot Credits Guide for credit consumption requirements.
claims.quote: Copilot credit consumption requirements are described in the Microsoft Copilot Credits Guide.
